metadata.title: Depth based on translates of a convex body: geometry, floating bodies, and empirical theory
metadata.abstract: For a fixed full-dimensional convex body $K\subset\mathbb R^d$, we study the $K$-depth of a point $y$ with respect to a probability measure $\mu$ by comparing the masses of translates of $K$ that fail to contain $y$. Its upper level sets are intersections of high-mass translates of $K$, and hence are convex and admit an exact representation as Minkowski erosions. We distinguish the closed core determined by the maximisers of the translation-mass function from the effective support on which the depth exceeds its unavoidable baseline. We establish continuity, affine equivariance, comparison with halfspace (Tukey) depth, and normal-cone and smoothness criteria. For uniform measures on convex bodies, the regions coincide exactly with the ball floating bodies of Schütt, Werner and Yalikun; for positive continuous densities they coincide with the weighted ball floating bodies of Werner and Yalikun. For dilates $tK$, the depth converges to a depth generated by the tangent cones of $K$ as $t \to \infty$; for smooth $K$ this limit is Tukey's halfspace depth, whereas nonsmooth testing bodies can produce a genuinely different limit. The worst-case maximal $K$-depth is exactly $1/h_T(K)$, where $h_T(K)$ is the Helly number of the family of translates of $K$. Under a uniform interior rolling-ball condition and compact support and having zero mass on hyperplanes, the convergence to halfspace depth is monotone and uniform with an explicit error bound. If the density is bounded by $L$, then this bound is of order $O(t^{-1})$ and this order is sharp. We also record that the dependence on the testing body is not monotone in general, while Hausdorff perturbations of $K$ give stable depth functions and regions at regular levels. Finally, we prove uniform consistency and pointwise weak limits for empirical $K$-depth, including the non-Gaussian limit caused by nonunique active translates.

analysis.topic: 度量测度几何、极限与奇异空间
analysis.workSummary: 研究由凸体平移质量定义的统计深度，以 Minkowski 腐蚀刻画上水平集，关联浮体与 Helly 数，并分析大尺度极限、稳定性及经验弱收敛。
techniques: 凸体平移与 Minkowski 腐蚀
analysis.breakthrough: 统一几何浮体和统计深度，并区分光滑与非光滑测试体的不同极限。
analysis.limitations: Tukey 深度极限及单调一致收敛需相应光滑、滚动球和测度假设；一般测试体并不单调。 当前数学解读依据摘要，尚未逐步审读证明。

analysis.priorityReason: 对凸几何与稳健统计交叉研究实用。
